title: Ladakh with Hanle and Tso Moriri in 10 Days: Nubra, Turtuk, Pangong and the Dark-Sky Reserve
meta_title: Ladakh Hanle and Tso Moriri Tour 10 Days
meta_description: 10-day Ladakh itinerary: Sham Valley, Nubra and Turtuk, Pangong Lake, two nights in Hanle's dark-sky reserve, Tso Moriri and Tso Kar on the way back to Leh.
tagline: Ladakh's lakes, the border villages and India's darkest skies
facts: Leh 3, Nubra 2, Pangong 1, Hanle 2, Tso Moriri 1
About 5,360 m on the passes; Hanle about 4,300 m
intro: The grand Changthang loop. After Nubra and Turtuk and a night at Pangong, you follow the frontier road through Chushul to Hanle, a village of the Changpa herders with a 17th-century monastery and one of the world's highest observatories, inside India's first dark-sky reserve. Two nights there leave time for the stars, then Tso Moriri and the salt lake of Tso Kar on the way back to Leh.

faqs.a: Rules for Hanle change; at times it has been open only to Indian citizens. We confirm the current position when you enquire and arrange any permit.

faqs.q: Is this trip too high for us?
faqs.a: It spends four nights above 4,200 m. It suits fit adults who have been to altitude before. For a gentler trip, choose the 6- or 8-day Ladakh plans.

faqs.q: When is the best night for stars?
faqs.a: In the week either side of the new moon. Tell us your dates and we will place the Hanle nights to suit.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

price_note: Contact us for a personalised quote for your dates, flights and hotel choice.

good_to_know.title: Altitude comes first
good_to_know.text: Leh is at about 3,500 m. Rest completely on the first day, drink 3 to 4 litres of water a day, avoid alcohol and smoking, and climb slowly. Ask your doctor about Diamox before you travel. Tell us about heart, lung or blood-pressure conditions before booking.

good_to_know.title: Phones
good_to_know.text: Only postpaid connections from other states work in Ladakh; prepaid SIMs from outside do not. Jio and Airtel postpaid have the widest coverage. Signal is weak or absent at Pangong, Tso Moriri and in Zanskar.

good_to_know.title: Layers, sun and monasteries
good_to_know.text: Even in summer it can be below zero on the passes. Carry a down jacket, cap, gloves, sunglasses and strong sunscreen. In monasteries cover shoulders and knees, remove hats, walk clockwise and ask before photographing monks.

good_to_know.title: Cash
good_to_know.text: ATMs work in Leh and Kargil only, and not always. Carry enough cash for the whole trip outside Leh. UPI works where there is signal.

good_to_know.title: UPI, cards and cash
good_to_know.text: UPI works almost everywhere, even at small stalls. Keep some cash in INR 100 and 200 notes for temples, parking, tips and places where the network is weak.

good_to_know.title: Temple and shrine etiquette
good_to_know.text: Cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes where asked, and carry socks for hot stone floors. Leather belts and bags are not allowed inside some Jain and Hindu temples. Ask before photographing people and inside shrines.

good_to_know.title: Water and street food
good_to_know.text: Drink sealed bottled or filtered water only. Choose busy stalls where food is cooked in front of you, and skip cut fruit and ice from roadside stalls.

good_to_know.title: Plugs and tipping
good_to_know.text: Plugs are Indian three-pin and two-pin, 230 volts. Tipping drivers and guides about INR 300 to 500 a day is appreciated.

dining_intro: India is the easiest country in the world for vegetarian and Jain travellers. We send your dietary brief to every hotel, and your driver knows clean, pure-vegetarian restaurants on each road day.
dining_avoid: Ask for food cooked fresh and tell the kitchen clearly if you eat Jain: no onion, garlic, ginger, potato or other root vegetables. Many dishes start with an onion-garlic base even when the menu says vegetarian.
food_card: Hum shuddh shakahari (Jain) hain. Pyaz, lahsun, adrak, aloo, gajar ya koi bhi zameen ke neeche ki sabzi nahi. Ande nahi. Kripya taaza banaiye. Dhanyavaad.
